shell.sampleHint: Fictitious company, people, documents and figures
shell.how: What is real and what is simulated?
real: The engine runs the workflow step by step with the sample you pick: it fills {{field}} templates, evaluates conditions, looks up the sample sheets and applies the rules.
Retries with growing waits, and "To review" cases you can retry, approve, mark as handled or discard.
A step's JavaScript code really runs, isolated in your browser.
Add, move, duplicate and delete steps; versions; templates; export the history as CSV and import or export the workflow as JSON.
Everything is saved in this browser (localStorage) until you reset the demo.
sim: The company, its suppliers, customers, invoices and figures are fictitious.
Connectors (email, spreadsheets, accounting software, CRM, payment gateway, WhatsApp) are not connected to anything: nothing is sent or charged.
The "AI" uses fixed rules (XML parsing, keywords and templates); it does not call any model.
Step timings are simulated and waits are shortened.
This month's runs and savings combine a sample pace with what you run here.
tour: Press "Run" with the matching invoice and watch each step on the canvas and in Runs.
Pick invoice FE-10234 (does not match) and run it: the case lands in "To review".
Open "Review cases" and approve or discard the exception.
Change the condition's tolerance or add a step from the palette and run again.
Save a version and try another template (collections or leads).
shell.resetBody: Your workflows, versions, runs and cases are deleted and today's sample data comes back.
shell.resetDone: The demo is back to the sample data.

palette.title: Step palette
palette.hint: Click to add after the selected step, or drag onto the canvas.

trigger_email.name: Incoming email
trigger_email.desc: Fires when an email reaches the mailbox (simulated).
trigger_email.help: Trigger. In the demo, each sample brings an email with the electronic invoice attached (XML). In your project it connects to your real mailbox with read-only access.

trigger_webhook.name: Web form
trigger_webhook.desc: Fires when your site submits a form.
trigger_webhook.help: Trigger. In the demo, the samples are contact forms already submitted. In your project, your site calls a secure workflow address.

trigger_schedule.name: Schedule
trigger_schedule.help: Trigger. Runs at the chosen time and days. In the demo, each sample is one receivables customer checked by that run.

trigger_chat.name: WhatsApp message
trigger_chat.help: Trigger. In the demo the messages are samples and there is no WhatsApp connection. In your project it uses WhatsApp Business with your company's line.

ai_extract.name: Read invoice
ai_extract.desc: Extracts tax ID, number, date, VAT and total from the XML.
ai_extract.help: In the demo the data is read from the XML with fixed rules, and confidence drops if fields are missing, if the tax ID check digit does not match or if subtotal + VAT does not add up to the total. Below the minimum, the case goes to "To review". In your project an AI model does it.

ai_classify.name: Classify message
ai_classify.desc: Assigns a category and detects the city.
ai_classify.help: In the demo it classifies by keywords: one line per category in the format "category: word, word". A category with no words is the fallback. It also detects the city if it appears in the text. In your project an AI model does it.

ai_draft.name: Draft text
ai_draft.desc: Writes a message with the case data.
ai_draft.help: In the demo it fills the template with the data ({{field}}); if a value is missing, the step fails and says which. In your project an AI model writes from this guide.

ai_rag.name: Ask the assistant
ai_rag.desc: Answers with company policies and cites the source.
ai_rag.help: In the demo it looks for the answer by keywords in four sample policies and cites the source; if nothing matches, the case goes to a person. In your project it is KopTup's RAG assistant with your documents.

app_sheet.name: Look up spreadsheet
app_sheet.desc: Finds a row by a column value.
app_sheet.help: Searches one of the three sample sheets (purchase orders, receivables and customers) for the row whose column matches the value. If it is not found, the case goes to "To review".

app_accounting.name: Post to accounting software
app_accounting.desc: Creates the payable or the receipt (simulated).
app_accounting.help: In the demo it validates the party and the amount and generates a sequential document number, but it does not connect to any accounting software. In your project it connects to yours through its API.

app_crm.name: Create CRM contact
app_crm.help: In the demo it checks whether the email already exists in the customers sheet (then it updates it) and assigns an ID; it does not connect to any CRM.

app_payment.name: Create payment link
app_payment.desc: Generates a payment link with a due date (simulated).
app_payment.help: In the demo the link is a sample (pagos.example) and charges nothing. In your project it connects to the payment gateway you use.

app_http.name: HTTP call
app_http.help: In the demo it does not go out to the internet: it validates the address and the JSON and replies with an echo of what you would send.

notify_chat.name: Send message
notify_chat.desc: Via WhatsApp or the team chat (simulated).
notify_chat.help: In the demo nothing is sent: it shows the message with the data filled in. WhatsApp requires a valid Colombian mobile number (10 digits starting with 3).

notify_email.name: Send email
notify_email.desc: Email to the customer or the team (simulated).
notify_email.help: In the demo no email is sent: it validates the address and shows the final text.

logic_condition.name: Condition (if / else)
logic_condition.desc: Compares two values and picks the path.
logic_condition.help: Compares the value with the one in "Against". "Is approximately equal to" accepts the % difference set in the tolerance. If it fails, the case goes to "To review" or the workflow ends without doing anything else.

logic_wait.name: Wait
logic_wait.desc: Pauses the workflow for some minutes.
logic_wait.help: In your project the workflow pauses for the given minutes. In the demo the wait is logged but skipped, so you are not kept waiting.

logic_assign.name: Assign by rule
logic_assign.desc: Picks an owner from a table.
logic_assign.help: One line per rule in the format "value = owner". The "* = …" line is the default rule. Case and accents are ignored.

code_js.name: JavaScript code
code_js.desc: Computes something with your own code.
code_js.help: The code really runs in your browser, isolated (no access to the page or the internet) with a 1.5-second limit. It receives "datos" and whatever you return goes to the next step.

code_map.name: Map fields
code_map.desc: Builds a new object from the data.
code_map.help: One line per field in the format "name = {{field}}". Use it to shape the data the way another system expects.

retry.intro: If the step fails with a temporary error (for example, the system replies 429), it is tried again with a growing wait.
retry.after: If retries run out, the run fails and the case stays in "To review" so you can retry it by hand.

test.note: Runs the previous steps with the sample and then this step. It is not added to the history.
test.blocked: The sample did not reach this step: it stopped at "{step}".

templates.title: Process templates
templates.subtitle: Sample workflows for a distributor. Using one creates a new workflow you can edit.

desc.invoices: Reads the electronic invoice that arrives by email, compares it with the purchase order and posts it as an account payable. If it does not match, it goes to review.
desc.collections: Every morning it checks receivables, creates a payment link and sends a WhatsApp reminder to customers with overdue invoices.
desc.leads: Classifies messages from the site's form, assigns a sales rep by city, creates the CRM contact and replies to the customer. Complaints go to review.
desc.assistant: Answers WhatsApp questions with the company's policies and cites the source. What the assistant does not know goes to a person.
desc.blank: Start with a web form as the trigger and build the workflow from the palette.

templates.note: All templates use sample data and simulated connectors. In your project we build them with your systems and your rules.

code.title: Code editor · {name}
code.subtitle: JavaScript that really runs in your browser, isolated and offline (up to {seconds} s).
code.help: Use "datos" to read what arrived (for example, datos.factura.total) and return an object. Tab inserts two spaces.
code.timeout: Stopped: it took longer than {seconds} s.
code.noInput: The input could not be computed.
code.blocked: The sample does not reach this step: it stopped at "{step}".
code.discardBody: Your code changes will be lost.

json.intro: You can download this workflow, edit it and import it back as a new workflow.
json.note: If you need a connector that is not in the palette, we build it in your project.
